title: Species Identification Workflow
text:
The original pollen detection pipeline handles generalized “pollen” tracking by treating everything equally as class 0. The Species Specific Pipeline introduces a secondary Stage 2 Classification network allowing us to categorize up to 45 different species per sample recursively mapping to the species_manifest.csv ground truth.


Because creating a single complex multi-class instance segmentation model requires immaculate datasets that track every overlapping object concurrently, the {{PROJECT_TITLE_CASE}} project splits logic into isolated loops:

Stage 1 Segmenter: Locates arbitrary pollen grains rapidly.
Stage 2 Classifier: Identifies the biological species directly from the bounded crops.






%%{init: {'theme': 'dark'}}%%
graph TD
  subgraph Stage 1
    A["Raw .czi Scans"] --> B["General Segmenter Model"]
    B --> C["Pollen Instance Masks"]
  end
  subgraph Stage 2
    C -->|extract_crops.py| D["Classification Dataset"]
    D -->|train_species.py| E["YOLOv8-cls Classifier Model"]
  end
  subgraph Feedback Loop
    E -->|inference_species.py| F["Active Learning UI Dataset"]
    F -->|Manual Fixes| G["dataset_species_curated/"]
    G -.->|Retrain| D
  end










If you have already generated generic detection boxes across your base biological datasets, you can slice these annotations natively into pristine crops ready for classification using extract_crops.py.
python src/extract_crops.py \
    --src Species_model/Training_data \
    --out dataset_species \
    --pad 0.1 \
    --split 0.8
This transforms segmented masks directly into standard dataset_species/train/<SpeciesCode> ImageNet structures compatible out-of-the-box with YOLOv8 Classification networks.




Native image classification trains faster and stronger than its segmentation counterparts. Execute the new wrapper script bridging yolov8n-cls weights with heavily augmented sweeps:
python src/train_species.py --dataset dataset_species
Outputs dynamically deploy to models/species_classifier/latest.pt ensuring recursive compatibility downstream.




The native inference_species.py script replaces czi_ingest.py when investigating novel, untouched samples.
This script parses all raw .czi microscopy files sequentially applying Stage 1 and Stage 2 models concurrently:
python src/inference_species.py \
    --root /path/to/czi/scans \
    --out ActiveLearning_Outputs \
    --model-seg models/general_pollen/latest.pt \
    --model-cls models/species_classifier/latest.pt



📊 summary_results.csv: A dense table specifying exactly [CZI_File, Tile, Species, Confidence, Area_um2] summarizing massive biological volumes.
🗺️ overview_{name}_labeled.jpg: A macro map detailing spatial distribution of every instance mapped by species!
🗂️ UI Dataset Format: Saves instances logically grouped (Images, Labels, Vizualization) explicitly built for immediate manual feedback.






Our AI improves only via your oversight. Start the frontend interface to manually vet species derivations:
python active_learning_ui.py
# → http://127.0.0.1:5001
Once in the inspector: 1. Use the “Filter by True Source Species” dropdown. Because the UI natively parses your dataset against species_manifest.csv, it perfectly isolates your newest target crops dynamically (even if the model grouped them into the wrong predictive folder initially). 2. Scan the visualized crops. 3. The “Correct Species Identity” is automatically pre-filled for you natively from the source filename! 4. Upon validating using [Right Arrow], the framework will natively physically crop and drop that corrected target directly into dataset_species_curated/train/<Species> feeding seamlessly right back into Step 2 for the next cycle.

title: {{PROJECT_TITLE_CASE}} Pollen Detection Pipeline
text: Welcome to the documentation for the {{PROJECT_TITLE_CASE}} Pollen Detection project. This pipeline is designed to handle high-resolution .czi (Zeiss) microscopy scans, segment individual pollen grains, and classify them by species using state-of-the-art YOLOv8 Instance Segmentation architectures.

title: {{PROJECT_TITLE_CASE}} Pollen Detection Pipeline
text:
1 🚀 Key Features

High-Resolution Tiling: Effortlessly process scans larger than 20,000 pixels by decomposing them into manageable training tiles.
Max-Z Projection: Automated MIP reduction to consolidate focus levels without losing detail.
Rigorous 80/10/10 Split: The pipeline enforces a strictly isolated 10% Test dataset, guaranteeing totally unbiased post-training evaluation metrics.
Automated Negative Filtering: 100% automated ingestion of purely empty background images to hyper-penalize false-positive debris detections.

title: {{PROJECT_TITLE_CASE}} Pollen Detection Pipeline
text:
2 📦 Data Storage Policy
To keep the repository lightweight and efficient, large datasets and model weights are not stored on GitHub. Instead, they are synchronized with the CESNET S3 (S3.cl4.du.cesnet.cz) storage.

Source Scans: Stored in s3://bucket/{{S3_PREFIX}}/detect_images/
YOLO Datasets: Stored dynamically via s3://bucket/{{S3_PREFIX}}/Staged_area/ and s3://bucket/{{S3_PREFIX}}/Staged_negatives/
Models: Stored reliably in s3://bucket/{{S3_PREFIX}}/trained_models/

title: {{PROJECT_TITLE_CASE}} Pollen Detection Pipeline
text:
3 🏷️ Roboflow Annotation
While the pipeline relies heavily on high-throughput automated slicing and pseudo_label.py scripts natively, the human-in-the-loop manual curation for the base general pollen model is hosted externally. You can review, correct, and track the instance-segmentation polygon masks online:
Roboflow: Pollen Lazy Labeling

title: {{PROJECT_TITLE_CASE}} Pollen Detection Pipeline
text:
5 🤖 Deploying a New Project
This repository serves as a master template. To quickly adapt it for a new specific project, you can leverage the built-in AI agent workflow.
Simply open this repository in VS Code, invoke the AI agent, and paste the following prompt:

“Please run the /adapt_project workflow to configure this Pollen Detection Template for my new project.”

The agent will prompt you for the new Project Name, Target Pollen Species List, S3 Bucket details, and GitHub Organization, and will cleanly automate the deployment by renaming configurations and rewriting manifests.

title: {{PROJECT_TITLE_CASE}} Pollen Detection Pipeline
text:
6 📖 Get Started
Check the following sections to get up and running:

Ingestion Tutorial: How to convert your first .czi folder.
Training: Set up GPU training using src/train_pollen.py.
Pseudo-Labeling: Auto-annotate tiles using src/pseudo_label.py.


Project maintained by Jakub Štenc (CESNET / Prague).

title: Ingestion Guide
text: The CZI Ingestion Pipeline converts raw Zeiss .czi scans into 640x640 JPG tiles formatted for YOLO training.

title: Ingestion Guide
text:
1 🏗️ Prerequisites
Ensure you have initialized the virtual environment:
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
# Use the IPv4 wrapper if you experience network hangs
python3 pip_ipv4.py install -r requirements.txt

title: Ingestion Guide
text:
2 📂 Source Data Structure
The script expects a directory structure where species codes are embedded in folder names:
/path/to/data/
├── Ran_ado/
│   ├── Source/
│   │   ├── scan_001.czi
│   │   └── scan_002.czi
├── Ran_rep/
│   └── ...

title: Ingestion Guide
text:
3 🛠️ Running the Ingest

3.1 Option A: Kubernetes Cluster (S3 Upload)
Best for large batches. This utilizes the cluster’s RAM to process all files and uploads a zipped .zip file archive to S3.
python k8s/deploy_czi.sh


3.2 Option B: Local Execution (Direct to Cloud Mount)
Best for bypassing S3 staging zip files and generating tiles directly onto a mounted drive for immediate Roboflow access.
# Ensure you are using the virtual environment
source .venv/bin/activate

python src/czi_ingest.py \
    --root /home/meow/cesnet_cloud/bucket/{{S3_PREFIX}}/Source/ \
    --out /home/meow/cesnet_cloud/bucket/{{S3_PREFIX}}/pollen_czi_v1 \
    --channels 0 1 2 \
    --grayscale


3.3 Key Parameters







Flag
Description




--root
Deepest root directory to scan for .czi files


--out
Target directory for images, labels, and data.yaml


--channels
Indices of fluorescence channels to use for R, G, B


--grayscale
Forces output to neutral grayscale instead of red (critical for manual Roboflow annotation)


--split
Train/Val ratio (e.g. 0.8 = 80% training data)


--dry-run
Preview the file list without writing to disk

title: Ingestion Guide
text:
4 📐 Resolution & Scaling
The pipeline automatically extracts the PhysicalSizeX metadata from the CZI. This is crucial for: 1. Scaling measurements in the final analysis. 2. Filtering debris based on physical area (pollen grains are typically 10–100µm).
Currently, the {{PROJECT_TITLE_CASE}} scans processed show a resolution of ~0.88 µm/px.
